# Domain boundaries and privacy

## Legal document workflows

- Treat public government guidance as a source for candidate process descriptions, not as a replacement for professional review.
- Do not infer case eligibility, legal deadlines, mandatory form fields, filing instructions, or outcomes unless verified against applicable current authoritative sources and reviewed for intended usage.
- Distinguish `draft for human review` from `ready to submit` and `submitted`; do not submit documents without an authorized and independently confirmed action.
- Keep jurisdiction, form revision, applicability date, and source revision in the specification. Mark unavailable or stale sources as unverified.
- Avoid confidential client inputs in public examples; use placeholders and synthetic data.

## Construction / quantity surveying workflows

- Keep contract scope, quantity, design information, construction method, site safety, and approval authority distinct; a QS's statements may not constitute an instruction to build or an approved method statement.
- Record drawing/BOQ revisions and disputed/unknown scope without resolving them automatically.
- Do not generate an executable site instruction or claim work is authorized based on AI inference.

## Confidential information, reviewers and audit trail

- Respect access permissions; do not upload customer files or case data to unauthorized model or review services.
- Do not assume third-party AI providers have the same confidentiality terms.
- Record who reviewed which artifact version and when only when that identity is known and permitted.
- Use redacted and synthetic example data when sharing an open-source test case.
